audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Gnar six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage anywhere read Kassadin - while the prose directly beneath it says the 2+ items stage is 'Your power window', late says "it's why the matchup is yours", and whys[6] says 'the lane finally flips to you'. Three sources, two answers.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 58.82% over 17 games. The shape is right - Gnar bullies levels 1-5 with a 1100-range Boomerang Throw against a 650-range Null Sphere - but a chart with no Kassadin stage at all cannot explain a winning matchup, and it contradicts its own text at the last stage.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Kassadin in both layers so the chart's tail matches whys[6] and the late-game prose. Levels 1-5 left with Gnar and Level 6 left as Skill: those match the text and the range gap. First item left with Gnar and its full-layer 'why' rewritten, because whys[5] and the phase card were arguing with each other there too.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike is described by name only - 'track his rage bar', 'Riftwalk is a survival spike' - with no cooldown attached to any of them, so the reader is told what to watch and never told how long the window lasts.
audit.why: The numbers are what make this lane playable. GNAR! is 90/60/30s but gated behind a full Rage bar, so it is a resource not a timer. Boomerang Throw is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and the cooldown is reduced only if he catches it, which means a boomerang he cannot recover is a genuine 16-second window at rank 1. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s - at rank 1 you get one blink out, at rank 3 you blink faster than he can reposition, which is the actual mechanism behind the 2+ items flip.
audit.corrected: Boomerang Throw's 16s and the catch-refund added to the Lvl 1-3 spike; GNAR!'s 90/60/30s and Riftwalk's 5s-to-2s spread added to the cooldown block and to mid/late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. First, breakdown.late tells you to 'Q-silence the counterplay' - Null Sphere has no silence. Second, early tells you to "hold Null Sphere's shield to block his poke", but the shield absorbs magic damage and Gnar's boomerang, autos and Hyper procs are all physical, so the page hands you a defensive plan that cannot fire.
audit.why: Riot's Null Sphere text is damage, channel interrupt, and a shield that absorbs MAGIC damage - no silence anywhere. The interactions the page actually needed and never printed: Void Stone ignores unit collision, so Kassadin walks straight through his own wave to break Gnar's firing line, which matters against a champion whose entire early game is a 1100-range line. And Mega Gnar's Boulder Toss stops on the first unit hit, so a wave between you and Mega Gnar eats his engage tool outright.
audit.corrected: Silence removed; the shield-vs-physical mismatch stated honestly and the Q re-tasked to last-hits; Void Stone's collision-ignore and Boulder Toss's first-unit stop added.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (P: 'ignores unit collision'; Q: shield 'absorbs magic damage')
champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (Q Mega: 'stops on the first unit hit')

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no cooldowns - it repeated 'track his rage bar like a cooldown' and then said the ult 'answers fights, not waves'.
audit.why: The three numbers that decide the lane are GNAR! 90/60/30s, Boomerang Throw 16s at rank 1 with a catch refund, and Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s.
audit.corrected: All three written into the cooldown block, with the point that Riftwalk is raced rather than waited out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere about GNAR!'s wall requirement, though 'wall-stun' is named four times across the two layers.
audit.why: GNAR! throws everything around him in a direction, and only enemies that HIT A WALL are stunned and take bonus damage. In open ground it is a displacement, not a stun - which is exactly the information that tells you where to stand.
audit.corrected: Added to the Key Ability Interactions block: fight in the open, where his R is a shove rather than a stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (R: 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned')

edits.before: Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q) outranges everything you have, and his Hyper (W) passive procs bonus damage on every third auto; you only have Null Sphere (Q), so you can't trade back — soak XP and grab safe CS while you bleed.
edits.after: Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q) outranges everything you have, and Hyper (W) turns his third hit into bonus damage and speed. His Q is 16s at rank 1 and refunds only if he catches it - step up on a boomerang he cannot recover.

edits.before: Concede levels 1-3 — this is one of your worst openings. Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q) outranges your Null Sphere (Q) by a mile, and his Hyper (W) passive adds bonus damage on every third auto, so even his hops chip you for free while your only answer is a short-range, mana-hungry Q. Don't walk up to last-hit into the boomerang; soak XP, take the CS you can safely grab, and hold Null Sphere's shield to block his poke rather than throwing it to trade. Watch his Rage bar — never stand in the wave when it's near full or his transform punishes you instantly.
edits.after: Concede levels 1-3 - this is one of your worst openings. Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q) reaches 1100 units against your 650, and Hyper (W) adds bonus damage and Move Speed on his third hit, so even his hops chip you for free while your only answer is a short-range, mana-hungry Q. Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic and every point of his poke is physical, so spend that Q on last-hits instead of hoarding it as armour. Void Stone ignores unit collision - walk through your own wave to break his firing line. Watch his Rage bar; never stand in the wave when it is near full.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are still a weather-the-storm window. Nether Blade (W) refunding mana (quintupled off champion hits) lets you actually farm under tower now, and a maxed Null Sphere eats one boomerang per trade, but you still lose every straight fight to his kite. At 6, Riftwalk (R) is a survival spike, not a kill spike — use it to blink out of a Wallop-into-GNAR! stun setup or dodge a gank, not to chase him down. The thing to truly fear is mega-Gnar: with a full bar his Wallop (W) and GNAR! (R) can pin you to a wall for his jungler, so respect the bar more than the champion.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are still a weather-the-storm window. Nether Blade (W) refunding mana (quintupled off champion hits) lets you actually farm under tower now, and a maxed Null Sphere eats one boomerang per trade, but you still lose every straight fight to his kite. At 6, Riftwalk (R) is 5s at rank 1 - one blink, so spend it escaping a Wallop-into-GNAR! setup or a gank, never chasing him down. The thing to truly fear is mega-Gnar: with a full bar his Wallop (W) and GNAR! (R) pin you to a wall for his jungler, so respect the bar more than the champion.

edits.before: This is the entire reason you suffered the lane — and it's why the matchup is yours. Once Riftwalk is maxed with Rod of Ages plus Nashor's or Lich Bane, you blink onto his backline and ramp Riftwalk's escalating stacks to burst his squishies, and his AD boomerangs simply don't threaten a scaled Kassadin. Stop trying to out-duel his kite in lane; instead roam, flank, and use Force Pulse (E) — refreshed by every ability cast around you — to chunk grouped fights. The only thing that catches you now is mega-Gnar's GNAR! wall-stun, so blink in from an angle he can't pre-aim.
edits.after: This is the entire reason you suffered the lane - and it's why the matchup is yours. Riftwalk drops to 2s at rank 3, so with Rod of Ages plus Nashor's or Lich Bane you blink onto his backline and ramp the escalating stacks faster than he can turn to face you. Stop trying to out-duel his kite in lane; roam, flank, and let Force Pulse (E) charge off the spells flying around you, then cone it into the cluster. The one thing that still catches you is GNAR! into a wall, so open every fight in open ground and blink from an angle he cannot pre-aim.

edits.before: With Riftwalk maxed and Nashor's/Rod of Ages online you blink-assassinate his squishies, and his AD poke can't stop scaled Kassadin — the lane finally flips to you.
edits.after: With Riftwalk at 2s and Rod of Ages online you blink-assassinate his squishies faster than he can turn, and his physical poke cannot stop scaled Kassadin - the lane flips to you.

edits.before: Rod of Ages turns survival into stats — the blink-trade pattern now genuinely chunks people.
edits.after: Rod of Ages turns survival into stats, but a full Rage bar plus his first item still wins the all-in.

edits.before: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Q-silence the counterplay, and leave before the fight even registers you.
edits.after: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Q-shield their answer, Force Pulse the cluster, and leave before it registers.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR! (Mega): matchup-defining — Mega all-in near walls — track his rage bar like a cooldown. Check it before every step-up. - Q shield is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - GNAR! (R) is 90/60/30s but gated on a full Rage bar - track the bar, not the timer. - Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 and only refunds if he catches it. - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3: race it, never wait it out.

edits.before: Track Gnar’s GNAR! (Mega): Mega all-in near walls — track his rage bar like a cooldown. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: GNAR! (R) stuns only enemies thrown into a wall, so fight in the open. Mega Boulder Toss stops on the first unit - keep the wave between you.

notes: Null Sphere was described as a silence in breakdown.late; Kassadin's Q has no silence (Riot: damage, channel interrupt, magic-absorbing shield). Separately, content.early told the reader to hold the Q shield against Gnar's poke - the shield is magic-only and Gnar's damage is physical, so the advice could never work; the Q is re-tasked to last-hits. Two interactions were absent from both layers and are now in: Void Stone ignores unit collision (walk through your own wave to break his 1100-range line) and Mega Gnar's Boulder Toss stops on the first unit hit (the wave eats his engage). GNAR! only stuns against a wall - the page said 'wall-stun' four times without ever saying that open ground defuses it. LEVEL CHART: no stage read Kassadin despite a 58.82% win rate and prose saying the lane 'finally flips to you'; 2+ items flipped in both layers. Ratings left untouched - this file's rating scale is internally inconsistent (both 'Kassadin 6/10' and 'Neeko 2/10' appear), so I changed side only and left mirror-fix.js to normalise the numbers.
